TRADEMARK COEXISTENCE AGREEMENT

This Trademark Coexistence Agreement (this "Agreement") is entered into as of April 6, 2026 (the "Effective Date") by and between Halcyon Provisions Company, a Delaware corporation with its principal place of business at 44 Bay State Road, Boston, Massachusetts 02215 ("Halcyon"), and Halcyon Cellars, LLC, a California limited liability company with its principal place of business at 1180 Silverado Trail, St. Helena, California 94574 ("Cellars"). Halcyon and Cellars are each a "Party" and together the "Parties".

RECITALS

A. Halcyon owns U.S. Trademark Registration No. 4,812,663 for HALCYON in International Class 30 for packaged dry goods, and uses that mark in connection with the products described in Schedule A (the "Halcyon Goods").

B. Cellars owns U.S. Trademark Application Serial No. 97/442,118 for HALCYON CELLARS in International Class 33 for wine, and uses that mark in connection with the products described in Schedule B (the "Cellars Goods").

C. Halcyon filed a Notice of Opposition against Cellars' application in Opposition No. 91/281,447 before the Trademark Trial and Appeal Board (the "Opposition").

D. The Parties have concluded that their respective marks can coexist without confusion if used as this Agreement provides, and they wish to settle the Opposition and to define the terms of that coexistence.

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants in this Agreement and other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:

1. DEFINITIONS

1.1 "Halcyon Mark" means the word mark HALCYON as registered in Registration No. 4,812,663 and any depiction of it.

1.2 "Cellars Mark" means the composite mark HALCYON CELLARS, used only in the form shown in Exhibit 1, in which "CELLARS" appears in the same font, color, and point size as "HALCYON" and on the same line.

1.3 "Field" means, for Halcyon, the Halcyon Goods and their advertising and promotion, and for Cellars, the Cellars Goods and their advertising and promotion.

2. CONSENT AND COEXISTENCE

2.1 Halcyon consents to Cellars' use and registration of the Cellars Mark in the United States for the Cellars Goods, and will not oppose, petition to cancel, or otherwise challenge the Cellars Mark for the Cellars Goods.

2.2 Cellars consents to Halcyon's use and registration of the Halcyon Mark in the United States for the Halcyon Goods, and will not oppose, petition to cancel, or otherwise challenge the Halcyon Mark for the Halcyon Goods.

2.3 Each Party acknowledges the other Party's ownership of, and the validity of, the other Party's mark within that Party's Field, and will not attack it directly or indirectly.

3. USE RESTRICTIONS

3.1 Cellars will use the Cellars Mark only in the form shown in Exhibit 1 and will not use HALCYON alone, and will not display HALCYON in a font, size, color, or position that gives it visual prominence over CELLARS.

3.2 Cellars will not use the Cellars Mark on or in connection with any food product, and will not expand its use beyond International Class 33 without Halcyon's prior written consent.

3.3 Halcyon will not use the Halcyon Mark on or in connection with any alcoholic beverage, and will not expand its use into International Class 33 without Cellars' prior written consent.

3.4 Neither Party will use the other Party's mark as a keyword, metatag, or domain name, or bid on it in paid search.

4. GEOGRAPHIC SCOPE

This Agreement applies in the United States and its territories. Each Party retains whatever rights it has outside the United States, and nothing here grants, limits, or admits anything about rights in any other country. If either Party seeks registration in a jurisdiction where the other Party's rights would block it, the Parties will negotiate in good faith a consent consistent with the allocation in Sections 2 and 3.

5. QUALITY AND CUSTOMER CONFUSION

5.1 Each Party will maintain the quality of the goods it sells under its mark at a level consistent with the quality prevailing on the Effective Date.

5.2 If either Party learns of actual confusion between the marks, it will notify the other Party within fifteen business days with the details known to it. The Parties will confer within thirty days after the notice and will cooperate in good faith on reasonable measures to reduce the confusion, which may include a disclaimer, a change in trade dress, or a change in channel of trade. Neither Party may unilaterally impose a measure on the other.

6. SETTLEMENT OF THE OPPOSITION

Within ten business days after the Effective Date, Halcyon will file a withdrawal of the Opposition with prejudice, and the Parties will file a joint stipulation to that effect with the Trademark Trial and Appeal Board. Each Party bears its own costs and attorneys' fees in the Opposition.

7. TERM AND TERMINATION

7.1 This Agreement takes effect on the Effective Date and continues in perpetuity, and its consents and covenants not to challenge survive any termination.

7.2 A Party may terminate this Agreement for the other Party's material breach if the breach is not cured within sixty days after written notice describing it. Termination does not revive the Opposition, does not withdraw a consent already given, and does not entitle either Party to challenge a registration issued in reliance on this Agreement. The use restrictions in Section 3 survive termination.

8. ASSIGNMENT

Neither Party may assign this Agreement except in connection with a transfer of the mark and the goodwill of the business associated with it, and then only if the assignee agrees in writing to be bound. Any purported assignment in violation of this Section is void. This Agreement binds and benefits the Parties and their permitted successors and assigns, and runs with the marks.

9. REMEDIES

The Parties acknowledge that a breach of Section 3 may cause irreparable harm for which damages are an inadequate remedy, and that the non-breaching Party may seek injunctive relief without posting a bond, in addition to any other remedy available at law or in equity.

10. GOVERNING LAW AND DISPUTES

This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of New York, without regard to its conflict-of-laws rules. The Parties consent to the exclusive jurisdiction and venue of the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York for any dispute arising out of or relating to this Agreement. Each Party waives any objection to that venue and any right to a trial by jury.

11. NOTICES

Notices under this Agreement must be in writing and are effective on receipt, delivered by hand, by nationally recognized overnight courier, or by certified mail, return receipt requested, to the addresses in the preamble, with a copy to each Party's counsel of record in the Opposition.

12. ENTIRE AGREEMENT; AMENDMENT

This Agreement is the entire agreement between the Parties on its subject matter and supersedes every prior or contemporaneous understanding on that subject. It may be amended only by a writing signed by both Parties. No waiver of any provision is effective unless in writing and signed by the Party against whom it is asserted, and no waiver is a waiver of any other or later breach.

13. COUNTERPARTS

This Agreement may be executed in counterparts, each of which is an original and all of which together are one instrument. A signature delivered electronically has the same effect as an original.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the Parties have executed this Agreement as of the Effective Date.
